story.title: Apple introduces M6 and M5 Ultra

draft:
Apple just shifted the AI compute baseline again.

The new M6 brings a 30 % jump in raw CPU throughput while the M5 Ultra doubles the neural engine cores. In practice that means training a 1‑billion‑parameter model on a laptop could finish in hours instead of days. For developers who have been off‑loading heavy inference to the cloud, the on‑device latency drop is a game‑changer.

What catches my eye is the unified memory bandwidth—over 1 TB/s across the die. It blurs the line between CPU, GPU, and dedicated AI accelerators, forcing us to rethink software stacks that still treat them as separate islands. I expect we’ll see more frameworks exposing a single API for all compute units, and a shift toward edge‑first AI pipelines.

Will you start prototyping larger models locally now that the hardware can keep up?
